strings.name: Bad Bunny
strings.summary: Born Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio, Bad Bunny moved from online uploads to international stages, combining reggaeton, Latin trap and Puerto Rican traditions. Working mainly in Spanish, he addresses identity, migration and island life. In 2026 Debí Tirar Más Fotos became the first Spanish-language Album of the Year Grammy winner; his Super Bowl halftime performance further expanded Latin music’s global visibility.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through Spanish-language music, reggaeton and Latin trap, he has global influence and raises international visibility for Puerto Rican culture and language.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Puerto Rico; raised in the Almirante Sur community of Vega Baja.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended the University of Puerto Rico at Arecibo in audiovisual communications while working in a supermarket and uploading music.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Spanish-language Grammy breakthrough
strings.highlights.h1.text: Debí Tirar Más Fotos won the 2026 Album of the Year Grammy, the first Spanish-language album to do so.
strings.highlights.h2.title: A global stage for Puerto Rican culture
strings.highlights.h2.text: Music, touring and the 2026 Super Bowl halftime show share Puerto Rican language and culture internationally.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Headlined Super Bowl halftime
strings.timeline.t1.text: Performed at Super Bowl LX, bringing Spanish-language music and Puerto Rican culture to a major television stage.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Won Album of the Year Grammy
strings.timeline.t2.text: Debí Tirar Más Fotos won the top album award, among his three Grammys that evening.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Released Debí Tirar Más Fotos
strings.timeline.t3.text: Combined Puerto Rican traditions, contemporary rhythms and reflections on migration.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Released Un Verano Sin Ti
strings.timeline.t4.text: Expanded his global audience and won the following year’s Best Música Urbana Album Grammy.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Spanish album topped US chart
strings.timeline.t5.text: El Último Tour del Mundo became the first all-Spanish album to lead the Billboard 200.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Released YHLQMDLG
strings.timeline.t6.text: The reggaeton-centered album strengthened his international presence and won the next year’s Latin Pop or Urban Album Grammy.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Released solo debut album
strings.timeline.t7.text: X 100pre turned earlier online singles success into a full-length album.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Gained attention with Diles
strings.timeline.t8.text: An online upload brought recording opportunities and a full-time music career.
